html:
The Celtic Tiger is the name for Ireland's economic boom from the mid 1990s to 2008, when it went from one of the poorer countries of western Europe to one of the richest.

Low corporate tax, an English-speaking young workforce, membership of the European Union since 1973 and its single market drew American technology and drug companies to Ireland. Wages and jobs grew fast, and for the first time in centuries more people came to Ireland than left it.

In the 2000s growth came more and more from a property bubble fed by cheap bank loans. When it burst in 2008, the banks collapsed and the state needed an international bailout in 2010. The economy recovered after 2013. The boom ended the long era of the Irish diaspora and helped change Ireland socially, as the marriage referendum showed. See the European Union.
sum: The Celtic Tiger is the name for Ireland's economic boom from the mid 1990s to 2008, when it went from one of the poorer countries of western Europe to one of the richest.
